title: "Alignment and quality control: Vvl and Rib ChIP-seq"
author: "Yermek Aiten"
output: html_document
---


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================
# Paired-end alignment: ttk, vvl, rib (and Twist if PE confirmed)
# ENCODE accessions: ENCSR362ZUH (ttk), ENCSR350VLI (vvl), ENCSR129UZN (rib)
# SLURM array, one element per sample (10 samples); bowtie2 then sort/index/RG/markdup
# Inputs: ${BASE_DIR}/01_fastq; outputs: 03_bam, 04_qc, 07_blacklist. Save as align_pe_controls.sh, run with sbatch
# ============================================================



set -euo pipefail

# ============================================================
# EDIT THESE PATHS
# ============================================================
BASE_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR"
DM6_IDX="$PROJECT_DIR/dm6"
PICARD_TMP="$PROJECT_DIR/tmp"
BLACKLIST="$PROJECT_DIR/dm6-blacklist.v2.bed"

# ============================================================
# SAMPLE TABLE
# Format: "SAMPLE_NAME  R1_ACCESSION  R2_ACCESSION"
# Each accession is a FASTQ file under ${BASE_DIR}/01_fastq/
# Controls are listed last (indices 8-9) so they can be skipped by
# downstream ChIP-only steps if needed.
# ============================================================
SAMPLES=(
  "RIB_rep1       ENCFF596NQN  ENCFF929RDR"
  "RIB_rep2       ENCFF489JKI  ENCFF889PVP"
  "RIB_control    ENCFF458LQH  ENCFF037LQP"
  "VVL_rep1       ENCFF895FAF  ENCFF061PMX"
  "VVL_rep2       ENCFF332TNC  ENCFF626ISZ"
  "VVL_control    ENCFF218OYW  ENCFF466TTY")

# ============================================================
# RESOLVE THIS ARRAY ELEMENT
# ============================================================
ENTRY="${SAMPLES[$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID]}"
SAMPLE=$(echo "$ENTRY" | awk '{print $1}')
ACC_R1=$(echo "$ENTRY" | awk '{print $2}')
ACC_R2=$(echo "$ENTRY" | awk '{print $3}')

FQ_R1="${BASE_DIR}/01_fastq/${ACC_R1}.fastq.gz"
FQ_R2="${BASE_DIR}/01_fastq/${ACC_R2}.fastq.gz"
SAM="${BASE_DIR}/03_bam/${SAMPLE}.sam"
BAM_RAW="${BASE_DIR}/03_bam/${SAMPLE}.bam"
BAM_RG="${BASE_DIR}/03_bam/${SAMPLE}.RG.bam"
BAM_SORTED="${BASE_DIR}/03_bam/${SAMPLE}.RG.sorted.bam"
BAM_RMDUP="${BASE_DIR}/03_bam/${SAMPLE}.rmdup.bam"
DUP_METRICS="${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.dup_metrics.txt"
FLAGSTAT="${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.flagstat.txt"

mkdir -p "${BASE_DIR}/03_bam" \
         "${BASE_DIR}/04_qc" \
         "${BASE_DIR}/07_blacklist" \
         logs

echo "========================================"
echo "SLURM array task : ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}"
echo "Sample           : ${SAMPLE}"
echo "R1               : ${FQ_R1}"
echo "R2               : ${FQ_R2}"
echo "CPUs allocated   : ${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}"
echo "========================================"

# Sanity check: both FASTQs must exist
if [[ ! -f "${FQ_R1}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: R1 FASTQ not found: ${FQ_R1}" >&2; exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "${FQ_R2}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: R2 FASTQ not found: ${FQ_R2}" >&2; exit 1
fi

# ============================================================
# STAGE 1, BOWTIE2 ALIGNMENT (paired-end)
# --no-mixed/--no-discordant drop unpaired or discordant alignments, -X 2000 allows inserts up to 2000 bp, -p uses all CPUs
# ============================================================
#conda activate phd

echo "[$(date)] Starting bowtie2 alignment..."


bowtie2 \
  -x "${DM6_IDX}" \
  -1 "${FQ_R1}" \
  -2 "${FQ_R2}" \
  --no-mixed \
  --no-discordant \
  -X 2000 \
  -p "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  -S "${SAM}" \
  2> "${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.bowtie2.log"


# ============================================================
# STAGE 2, SAM -> SORTED BAM
# Use all CPUs for sort; pipe avoids writing intermediate SAM to disk
# ============================================================
samtools sort \
  -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  -o "${BAM_RAW}" \
  "${SAM}"

rm -f "${SAM}"
samtools index -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" "${BAM_RAW}"

echo "[$(date)] Sort complete."

# ============================================================
# STAGE 3, ADD READ GROUPS
# ============================================================
picard -Djava.io.tmpdir="${PICARD_TMP}" \
  AddOrReplaceReadGroups \
  I="${BAM_RAW}" \
  O="${BAM_RG}" \
  RGID="${SAMPLE}" \
  RGLB=lib1 \
  RGPL=ILLUMINA \
  RGPU=unit1 \
  RGSM="${SAMPLE}"

echo "[$(date)] Read groups added."

# ============================================================
# STAGE 4, SORT AFTER READ GROUPS
# ============================================================
samtools sort \
  -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  -o "${BAM_SORTED}" \
  "${BAM_RG}"

rm -f "${BAM_RAW}" "${BAM_RG}"
echo "[$(date)] Sorted after RG."

# ============================================================
# STAGE 5, MARK AND REMOVE DUPLICATES
# For paired-end data, Picard uses mate information to identify duplicates
# correctly, no additional flags needed vs SE
# ============================================================
picard -Djava.io.tmpdir="${PICARD_TMP}" \
  MarkDuplicates \
  I="${BAM_SORTED}" \
  O="${BAM_RMDUP}" \
  M="${DUP_METRICS}" \
  REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true \
  ASSUME_SORTED=true

samtools index -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" "${BAM_RMDUP}"
rm -f "${BAM_SORTED}"
echo "[$(date)] Duplicates removed."

# ============================================================
# STAGE 6, MAPQ FILTER (>=30) + BLACKLIST REMOVAL
# For PE: -f 3 keeps only properly paired reads (both mates mapped,
# correct orientation). -F 3852 removes unmapped, secondary, QC-fail,
# supplementary reads. Combined with -q 30 this is the standard ENCODE
# PE ChIP-seq filter.
# ============================================================
CLEAN_BAM="${BASE_DIR}/07_blacklist/${SAMPLE}.clean.bam"

samtools view \
  -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  -b \
  -f 3 \
  -F 3852 \
  -q 30 \
  "${BAM_RMDUP}" \
  | bedtools intersect \
      -v \
      -abam stdin \
      -b "${BLACKLIST}" \
  > "${CLEAN_BAM}"

samtools index -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" "${CLEAN_BAM}"
echo "[$(date)] MAPQ filter and blacklist removal complete."

# ============================================================
# STAGE 7, FLAGSTAT ON CLEAN BAM
# ============================================================
samtools flagstat \
  -@ "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  "${CLEAN_BAM}" \
  > "${FLAGSTAT}"

echo "[$(date)] Flagstat written to ${FLAGSTAT}"
cat "${FLAGSTAT}"

# ============================================================
# STAGE 8, FRAGMENT SIZE ESTIMATION WITH bamPEFragmentSize
# Only meaningful for ChIP samples, not controls, but run on all for QC.
# ============================================================
#conda activate deeptools 2>/dev/null || true  # fall back to phd if no separate env

bamPEFragmentSize \
  -b "${CLEAN_BAM}" \
  --outRawFragmentLengths \
    "${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.frag_lengths.txt" \
  -o "${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.frag_hist.png" \
  -p "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}" \
  2> "${BASE_DIR}/04_qc/${SAMPLE}.fragsize.log"

#conda activate phd

echo "[$(date)] Fragment size estimation complete."
echo "[$(date)] === DONE: ${SAMPLE} ==="
```
